brief.headline: Offer to pay them in 15 days (freeing ₹26.60 L cash for us) in exchange for a 12% price cut — their cash is stuck 101 days (far longer than similar firms' 64d) and they borrow at 12.16%

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 12% price cut in exchange for paying them in 15 days instead of 30
priceAsk.target: A cut worth roughly 12.16% — the rate they pay to borrow money — because paying them 15 days early is worth that much to them
priceAsk.basis: Their cash is stuck for 101 days versus 64 days at similar firms, so getting paid early saves them borrowing cost at 12.16%. Our current price sits at the top of the fair market band (₹205–305/kg typical ₹250/kg), so there's room to move down while staying market-reasonable

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay them in 15 days (15 days faster than our current 30 days)
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: This costs us ₹26.60 L in cash, but we get it back as a price cut worth more

brief.financialLeverage: They're a ₹1064.86 Cr company, so our ₹6.47 Cr spend is only 0.61% of their revenue — we're tiny to them, so we can't bully on volume. But their finances are tight: they keep just 2.3% profit (similar firms keep 2.5%), they owe 1.25 times their own cash (₹282.62 Cr debt), and their cash is stuck for 101 days versus 64 at peers. They've had EPF payment delays and sit in the grey distress zone (Altman Z 2.36), with a middling CARE BBB+ rating and a weak 3/10 financial score. Cash is tight for them, so they'll value faster payment — but push gently, because squeezing a fragile supplier too hard risks our supply.

evidence.point: Their cash is stuck much longer than similar firms
They borrow money at a high rate
We're a very small customer to them
They carry heavy debt relative to their own cash
They sit in the grey financial zone and have payment delays
evidence.figure: Altman Z 2.36 (grey zone), EPF payment delays, CARE BBB+ rating, 3/10 score

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter, already supplies FDC in small volumes — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets (₹2758.00 Cr revenue, health C 59/100)

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant that makes both film and converts it — can second-source laminates at scale (₹16492.00 Cr revenue, health C 46/100)

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of global Constantia group, specialises in pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong second-source fit for our sachets (₹222.04 Cr revenue, health D 31/100)

risks: They sit in the grey distress zone (Altman Z 2.36) with EPF payment delays and a middling BBB+ rating — pushing too hard on price could tip a fragile supplier and hurt our supply
We're only 0.61% of their revenue, so we have little volume leverage — the ask must lean on the cash-timing win for them, not on our size
Their profit is just 2.3% — there's almost no margin to spare, so frame the price cut as funded by their borrowing-cost saving, not as squeezing profit
Interest coverage is thin at 1.94x — they're stretched servicing debt, so if we don't offer faster payment the price ask has no leg to stand on
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to help free up your cash by paying you in 15 days instead of 30 — and in return, we're looking for a price reduction that reflects the 12% borrowing cost you'll save.
